findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`, so the guard never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honours `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` is never called, so the `website.present?` check is dead code. `website_name` is always emitted as a key, with a nil value when there is no website. The template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the nil case, but the intended contract (omit the attribute when there is no website) is not enforced. Rename it to `include_website_name?`. Note that `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, which matters more (see the next finding).

findings.title: website_name leaks the website domain for restricted (TL0, anonymous) users
findings.body: `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` and is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. This is anti-spam behaviour for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers. The new `website_name` is derived from the same website but is not in that list, and its own `include_` hook is misnamed. The serializer therefore still returns the host and path for restricted users, and the profile template renders it as visible text. That defeats the restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`. The spec's `untrusted_attributes` list (spec line 11) also needs `website_name`, otherwise nothing guards against this regression.

findings.title: Client-side website_name goes stale after the website is edited
findings.body: The old `websiteName` was a computed property on `model.website`, so it updated immediately when the website changed. It is now a server-provided static attribute, `website_name`. `User.save()` sends `website` but on success only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response, so `website_name` is never refreshed. After a user edits their website in preferences and returns to the profile, the user route is not re-entered, so `findDetails` is not re-run. The profile then shows the old name next to the new `href`. If the website is cleared, the old name is still shown with an empty link. Update `website_name` from the save response, or keep deriving it on the client.

findings.title: website_name implementation is fragile and has edge-case quirks
findings.body: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal. It works today only because literals are not frozen, and it will raise FrozenError under `# frozen_string_literal: true`. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times per call; parse it once. For `http://example.com/` the result is `example.com/` with a dangling slash, and query strings and fragments are silently dropped. The duplicated ternaries make the three branches hard to follow. Extract a local `path` and a boolean `same_site`.

findings.title: Website-name specs miss the sibling-subdomain branch and edge cases
findings.body: The three specs cover different domain, same domain, and website domain as parent of the instance domain. They do not cover the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` sibling-subdomain branch. They also skip a website without a scheme or an unparseable URL (the `rescue nil` path), a blank website, a trailing-slash URL, and the untrusted/anonymous TL0 case where `website_name` should be hidden. Because of this, the missing `?` on `include_website_name` and the restricted-user leak go undetected.
